title: Adagrasib in Patients with KRAS G12C-Mutated Advanced Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer (KRYSTAL-1)
authors: Jänne PA, Riely GJ, Gadgeel SM, Heist RS, Ou SI, Pacheco JM
mesh_terms: Non-Small-Cell Lung Carcinoma, KRAS Protein, Targeted Therapy, Neoplasm Metastasis
abstract: Adagrasib is a covalent inhibitor of KRAS G12C that irreversibly traps KRAS G12C in its inactive GDP-bound state. In this Phase 2 cohort of the KRYSTAL-1 study, patients with previously treated KRAS G12C-mutant NSCLC received oral adagrasib 600 mg twice daily. Among 112 evaluable patients, objective response occurred in 43% of patients, with median duration of response of 8.5 months and median progression-free survival of 6.5 months. Acquired resistance mutations were identified in secondary KRAS switch-II pockets and bypass MET amplifications.

title: Sotorasib for Lung Cancers with KRAS p.G12C Mutation (CodeBreaK 100)
authors: Skoulidis F, Li BT, Govindan R, Barlesi F, Dingemans AC, Dy GK
mesh_terms: KRAS Inhibitor, NSCLC, Mutation Specific, Protein Binding
abstract: In the CodeBreaK 100 registrational phase 2 trial, oral sotorasib (960 mg once daily) demonstrated confirmed objective response in 37.1% of patients with pretreated KRAS G12C-mutated NSCLC. Disease control was observed in 80.6%. Median overall survival was 12.5 months. Genomic profiling of ctDNA at progression highlighted polyclonal resistance mechanisms including KRAS Y96D and parallel EGFR/HER2 pathway activations.

title: Molecular Mechanisms of Acquired Resistance to KRAS G12C Direct Inhibitors
authors: Tanaka N, Lin JJ, Li C, Ryan MB, Zhang J, Koyama S
mesh_terms: Drug Resistance, Neoplasm, Signal Transduction, Gene Amplification
abstract: Direct covalent KRAS G12C inhibitors achieve disease remission but duration is curtailed by drug resistance. We mapped structural genomic alterations in 38 clinical biopsies and CRISPR patient-derived models. Resistance frequently arises via secondary KRAS mutations that impair drug binding (G12D, G12V, Y96C, R68S) or through upstream RTK activation (MET, HER2) and downstream SHP2/SOS1 feedback loops, suggesting synergistic combination therapies with pan-KRAS or SHP2 blockers.

title: First-Line Pembrolizumab Plus Chemotherapy in PD-L1 High Metastatic NSCLC: 5-Year Outcomes
authors: Reck M, Rodríguez-Abreu D, Robinson AG, Hui R, Csőszi T, Fülöp A
mesh_terms: Pembrolizumab, Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors, Carcinoma, Non-Small-Cell Lung, Survival Analysis
abstract: Five-year follow-up of KEYNOTE-024 established first-line pembrolizumab monotherapy doubled 5-year overall survival rate versus platinum doublet chemotherapy (31.9% vs 16.3%, HR 0.62) in patients with metastatic NSCLC and PD-L1 tumor proportion score >=50%. Toxicity profile remained manageable with lower incidence of treatment-related grade 3-5 adverse events.

title: Lecanemab in Early Alzheimer's Disease: Clarifying Amyloid Clearance and Cognitive Decline
authors: van Dyck CH, Swanson CJ, Aisen P, Bateman RJ, Chen C, Gee M
mesh_terms: Alzheimer Disease, Amyloid beta-Peptides, Antibodies, Monoclonal, CDR-SB
abstract: In the Clarity AD phase 3 randomized controlled trial involving 1795 participants with early Alzheimer's disease, lecanemab reduced brain amyloid-beta burden on PET scans and led to a 27% slowing of clinical decline on the CDR-SB at 18 months compared to placebo (difference -0.45; P<0.001). Amyloid-related imaging abnormalities with edema (ARIA-E) occurred in 12.6% of the lecanemab group.

title: Donanemab in Early Symptomatic Alzheimer Disease (TRAILBLAZER-ALZ 2)
authors: Sims JR, Zimmer JA, Evans CD, Lu M, Ardayfio P, Sparks J
mesh_terms: Donanemab, Tau Proteins, Amyloid Clearance, iADRS
abstract: Donanemab significantly slowed clinical progression by 35.1% on the integrated Alzheimer Disease Rating Scale (iADRS) at 76 weeks in participants with early symptomatic Alzheimer disease and low-to-medium tau pathology. Brain amyloid plaque was cleared to normal physiological levels in 80% of patients by week 76, allowing treatment completion.

title: Bispecific Antibodies in Relapsed/Refractory Multiple Myeloma: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
authors: Kumar SK, Callander NS, Adekola K, Anderson LD, Baljevic M
mesh_terms: Multiple Myeloma, Bispecific Antibodies, BCMA, GPRC5D, Cytokine Release Syndrome
abstract: Meta-analysis of 14 clinical trials evaluating BCMAxCD3 and GPRC5DxCD3 bispecific T-cell engagers (teclistamab, elranatamab, talquetamab) demonstrated pooled overall response rate of 68.4% (95% CI: 63.2-73.6) in heavily pretreated relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma. Grade 3+ infections occurred in 41.2% and cytokine release syndrome in 67.5% (mostly grade 1-2).

title: Targeted Protein Degradation via PROTACs in Oncology: Mechanisms, Structural Chemistry, and Clinical Horizons
authors: Békés M, Langley DR, Crews CM
mesh_terms: Proteolysis Targeting Chimeric Chimeras, Ubiquitin-Protein Ligases, ARV-110, ARV-471
abstract: Proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTACs) hijack the intracellular ubiquitin-proteasome machinery to selectively eliminate disease-causing proteins rather than simply inhibiting their active sites. This review synthesizes pharmacokinetic, ternary complex cooperativity, and clinical data from first-in-human trials of ARV-110 (androgen receptor) and ARV-471 (estrogen receptor) in resistant prostate and breast cancer.

title: Tirzepatide Once Weekly for the Treatment of Obesity: The SURMOUNT-1 Trial
authors: Jastreboff AM, Aronne LJ, Ahmad NN, Wharton S, Connery L, Alves B
mesh_terms: GLP-1 Receptor Agonist, GIP Receptor, Weight Loss, Cardiovascular Risk
abstract: In this 72-week double-blind, randomized, controlled phase 3 trial, tirzepatide (dual GIP and GLP-1 receptor agonist) at 15 mg weekly yielded mean body weight reduction of -20.9% (-23.6 kg) compared to -3.1% in the placebo group. Substantial improvements in all prespecified cardiometabolic risk factors were documented.

title: Semaglutide and Cardiovascular Outcomes in Patients with Overweight or Obesity (SELECT)
authors: Lincoff AM, Brown-Frandsen K, Colhoun HM, Deanfield J, Emerson SS
mesh_terms: Semaglutide, Myocardial Infarction, Stroke, Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events
abstract: In the landmark SELECT trial of 17,604 non-diabetic overweight or obese patients with preexisting cardiovascular disease, once-weekly subcutaneous semaglutide 2.4 mg reduced the risk of primary composite endpoint (cardiovascular death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, or nonfatal stroke) by 20% (HR 0.80, 95% CI 0.72-0.90, P<0.001) over mean duration of 39.8 months.

title: Efficacy of BNT162b2 and mRNA-1273 Booster Vaccines against SARS-CoV-2 Omicron Subvariants
authors: Andrews N, Stowe J, Kirsebom F, Toffa S, Sachdeva R, Gower C
mesh_terms: mRNA Vaccines, SARS-CoV-2, Omicron, Neutralizing Antibodies
abstract: Nationwide cohort analysis evaluated vaccine effectiveness of homologous and heterologous mRNA boosters against symptomatic infection and hospitalization during Omicron wave. Vaccine effectiveness against hospitalization was 92% at 2-4 weeks post booster and sustained at 78% after 20+ weeks, highlighting durable cell-mediated and humoral protection.

title: In Vivo CRISPR-Cas9 Genome Editing with Lipid Nanoparticles for Transthyretin Amyloidosis
authors: Gillmore JD, Gane E, Taubel J, Kao J, Fontana M, Maitland ML
mesh_terms: CRISPR-Cas9, Lipid Nanoparticles, Transthyretin, Gene Knockout, Amyloid Neuropathy
abstract: NTLA-2001, an investigational in vivo CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing therapy targeting the TTR gene via liver-tropic lipid nanoparticles, achieved rapid and sustained serum TTR reductions of up to 93% following a single intravenous infusion in hereditary ATTR amyloidosis patients. Knockout was stable across 24 months of observation with benign safety profile.
